chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Billie Holiday and her dog Mister at Creole Pete's
summary: Danny describes Billie's circle, her dog Mister, and the ritual of feeding the boxer from a spoon at Creole Pete's.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: So I was at the Mad House. I told you about that Chicken Cock whiskey... So there I saw Billie for the first time. I never got to know Billie personally, because I had been involved with young ladies who knew Billie and I'd hear about Billie, and...um, from then on, she went on. But Billie always knew the right people. In fact, she knew too many right people. She knew the right people, the wrong people, and she always had a group of people with her, because she was a fascinating young lady.

You'd see Billie with maybe three Mexicans one night. Tomorrow you'd see her with some Chinese. Some cat from Georgia somewhere. You'd see her with some... Always with some people with them dark glasses. Later on you wouldn't see her with a man. You'd always see her with a dog. The last dog she had, his name was Mister. Yeah, Mister. She used to go to Creole Pete's Restaurant with Mister, and sit with Mister at a table, and if you were half-drunk and you looked over there, you would think it was some little midget or something sitting over there.
Creole Pete just passed recently, didn't he.
Yeah, I'm sorry to hear that. He was such a nice man.
Yeah. His boy gave him a hard time.
He was a Globetrotter, his son.

Billie used to go into Creole Pete's and eat, and she'd order ham-and-eggs, and she'd order hash-brown potatoes for her dog. And the dog would sit there, and she'd eat and feed the dog, and both of them eating out of spoons. Because she loved that dog. People would come in there and they'd give Pete hell. They'd say, "Well, goddamn, we're not eating that food off them plates, and no way we're eatin' behind no dog." But that was a ritual to see Billie, you know. Because the dog would be sitting up there... You know how a boxer dog is. He's sitting down, and if you look, it looks like...
A little fellow sitting over there or something.

[LAUGHS] Yeah. So they made her stop or get paper plates to feed that dog in. "I don't care who it is, Billie or... Man, I ain't gonna in here no more." A lot of people said that. Because she'd sit there feeding him, "All right, Mister, come on now, Mister, open your mouth." [LAUGHS]
